messages:
Kyra: hey team, first-week setup question — trying to get a consistent dev env on Windows (WSL2 + WSLg + VSCode Remote). hitting nodenv/asdf conflicts, gpg commit signing not picked up in VSCode, and 1password cli isn't persisting the session. Any recommended checklist?
Sam: welcome Kyra! :wave: quick Qs: are you using the Windows host for tooling or doing everything inside WSL?
Kyra: doing most inside WSL (Ubuntu). I installed Homebrew in WSL after following a blog and then added asdf. problem is VSCode terminal sometimes uses Windows PATH and picks the wrong node.
Marta: make sure VSCode opens the folder in WSL (Remote - WSL extension). that forces the shell to be the WSL user.
Marta: also ensure PATH order in your shell rc: for zsh/bash put asdf before system paths. e.g.
```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
source /etc/profile
```
Sam: add this: in VSCode settings set "terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.linux" to your shell (zsh) and restart the window.
Kyra: that helped but GPG signing still uses Windows gpg (I think). my git commits are unsigned in the remote-targeted VSCode UI.
Alex: for gpg you want the agent running in WSL. install gnupg inside WSL, import your key there, and set git config --global gpg.program /usr/bin/gpg. also ensure pinentry is installed so VSCode can prompt.
Alex: if you used a GPG key originally on mac/windows, export the private key and import to WSL: `gpg --export-secret-keys --armor YOURKEYID | gpg --import`
Marta: WSLg can complicate GUI pinentry but usually `sudo apt install pinentry-tty` or `pinentry-curses` and configure `gpg-agent.conf` with `pinentry-program /usr/bin/pinentry-curses`. works well in terminal flows.
Kyra: noted. what about 1Password CLI? I run `eval $(op signin)` but it expires and vscode can't use the op session for secrets (eg. REDWOOD_API_KEY).
Sam: two options: 1) use op session env and direnv to load env into shells, or 2) use 1Password SSH agent / secrets automation if you have enterprise seats.
Sam: basic direnv snippet:
```bash
eval "$(op signin my)"
# store REDWOOD_API_KEY in 1Password, then:
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(op read "op://Redwood/Dev/REDWOOD_API_KEY")
```
Marta: for persistence across restarts, you can script token refresh in .profile with proper TTL checks, but be careful with security. we prefer direnv + `.envrc` checked locally (not committed).
Kyra: should I set REDWOOD_API_KEY in repo .env.local? seems easier for dev, but obviously risky.
Alex: don't commit secrets. use `.env.local` in .gitignore or use direnv/op to inject. onboarding docs recommend `direnv` + `.envrc` per repo.
OnboardingBot: Hey Kyra — reminder: internal onboarding guide at https://intranet/redwood/onboarding/dev-setup has a WSL section and sample .envrc for the web repo.
Kyra: thanks! one lingering issue: docker-compose failing to pull images due to corporate CA (we have a company registry) — cert verify fails inside WSL.
Sam: got you — import the corporate root cert into WSL's CA store and into Docker Desktop (Settings -> Resources -> WSL Integration). inside WSL: `sudo cp /path/to/ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/company.crt && sudo update-ca-certificates`. restarted docker for me.
Marta: also ensure Docker Desktop uses WSL2 backend and the distro is enabled in Resources > WSL Integration.
Kyra: beautiful. last ask: any recommended VSCode extensions?
Alex: Remote - WSL, ESLint, Prettier, GitLens, Docker, and the Redwood snippets extension (we have a small set in the marketplace).
Kyra: thanks all — will follow the steps and ping if stuck. :thumbsup:
Sam: shout if you want a quick screen share, happy to pair and sort the GPG/1Password bits.
Marta: welcome aboard again!
Kyra: appreciate it everyone :heart:
